Let me analyze this ticket.

Donna Ball (E024) requests write access to Payroll.

Notes:
- Note 1 (ticket 1): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time
- Note 2 (ticket 1): employment type contractor, security training basic
- Note 3 (ticket 2): role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read, comment: Security DB confirms contractor with basic training, max out at read.

There's conflicting info: Note 1 says full_time, but later notes (2 and 3) say contractor with basic security training. The most recent note (ticket 2) confirms contractor with basic training.

Policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. If she were full_time Payroll Specialist, Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role, so admin would be allowed... actually full_time gets up to write, admin only if role owns system - so full_time Payroll Specialist could get admin for Payroll.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Current info says contractor with basic security training. So max is read. Requested write > max read, so grant max = read.

The recommendation from the security note is read. So decision: read.

Submit decision with read.
